mappings.note: One letter from the 26 equally likely letters, favourable if it is one of DELHI's five. Simple event, LO-3.
A single draw from the 90 two-digit numbers; 'multiple of 3 and not of 5' is a compound description of the event, not a compound experiment, so LO-3 rather than LO-4.
One ticket from 25, five of which win. Simple event, LO-3.
Tests x^2 < 2 on five equally likely numbers. Single draw, LO-3; the squaring is arithmetic, not a second stage.
Picks out P(E) + P(E-bar) = 1 from three wrong relations. The complement identity, LO-4; LO-2 covers the range, not this sum.
Two dice, sum a multiple of 4, requiring nine favourable pairs out of 36. A compound dice event, LO-4.
Counts vowels in ASSASSINATION for a single draw, then solves 6/(2x+1) = 6/13. The probability step is a simple event, LO-3; the equation is only algebraic dressing.
One fish from 14. Simple event, LO-3.

Two independent selections whose nine ordered pairs must actually be listed before the product condition can be tested. C-8.1-LO-4 (lists the sample space) leads because the enumeration is the work; LO-4 covers the compound structure, though its wording names only cards, dice and coins.
'No cash prize' is the complement of the 310 prize-bearing envelopes, found as 1000 - 310. The complement outcome, LO-4.
Assertion-reason: rejects P = 1.1 because probability lies in [0, 1]. The reason IS the range statement, so LO-2 and not LO-3, even though a face-card count appears in the working.
Multiples of 4 among 1 to 15. Simple event, LO-3.
Two coins, at most one head, over {HH, HT, TH, TT}. A compound coin event, LO-4.
One die, number below 3. Simple event, LO-3.
Square at most 1 over eleven equally likely integers. Single draw, LO-3.
One card, red king, 2 of 52. Simple event, LO-3.
Losing is the complement of winning, so P = 1 - 0.07. Pure complement-rule application, LO-4; no sample space is counted.
One card, red face card, 6 of 52. Simple event, LO-3.

Asks for the count of favourable outcomes rather than a probability, so C-8.1-LO-4 leads; the event is a complement ('not the ace of hearts'), hence LO-4. LO-3 would require a probability to be produced.
One die, odd and below 3. Simple event, LO-3.
Inverts the definition P = n(E)/n(S) to recover the number of bad eggs. Definition (LO-2) plus favourable count (C-8.1-LO-4); no probability is calculated, so LO-3 does not apply.
Same inverse structure: given probability and total, find the count of winning tickets held. Definition plus favourable count.
States that an impossible event has probability 0, the lower bound of the range. LO-2.
Primes among 1 to 100 for a single pick. Simple event, LO-3.
Sample space is the four one-digit primes; one is even. Simple event over a small equally likely set, LO-3.
